name: Alhambra Palace Hotel
positioning: Historic neo-Moorish palace hotel in Granada, founded by the Duke of San Pedro de Galatino and still managed by his heirs
best_for: Travelers who want a historic, Moorish-style base near the Alhambra
Guests interested in Granada's history, flamenco and intimate music

facts.text: In 1905 the Duke of San Pedro de Galatino decided to build the hotel, originally called The Hotel Casino Alhambra Palace.
The building's 'galatea orange' hue comes from the colour of iron-rich earth and shifts with the time of day, resembling the nearby Alhambra.
The exterior has a crenelated, curvilinear design likened to the walls of Avila.
The interior is neo-Moorish, with mirrors, mosaics, muqarnas and arches.
El Teatrillo, the hotel's Little Theater, stands where the duke's casino once was.
El Teatrillo's size suits chamber music, solo recitals and small performances.
In June 1922 the theater hosted the flamenco song contest known as the Concurso del Cante Jondo.
During the Civil War the hotel became a field hospital for three years.
Red crosses painted on the roof saved the building from aerial bombardment.
Since the early 1980s the duke's heirs have managed the hotel directly.
The hotel has hosted travellers, aristocrats, royalty and artists from around the world.
The hotel is at Plaza Arquitecto Garcia de Paredes 1 in Granada.

highlights.text: The hotel's theater hosted the Concurso del Cante Jondo flamenco song contest in June 1922.
A neo-Moorish interior of mirrors, mosaics, muqarnas and arches.
A 'galatea orange' facade, coloured by iron-rich earth, that changes with the time of day like the nearby Alhambra.
Red crosses painted on the roof during the Civil War saved the building from aerial bombardment.

considerations.text: The decor is ornate neo-Moorish, with mirrors, mosaics and arches, not a contemporary minimalist look.
WhataHotel notes the historic building has older room configurations.
WhataHotel notes parking is limited because of the hillside location.
